source.title: Derry Journal, 6 October 1937, p. 5 ("Derry municipal elections: yesterday's nominations (continued)"); Derry Journal, 6 October 1937, p. 5 ("Derry municipal elections: yesterday's nominations; no contests in any ward")
source.publisher: Derry Journal (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed (Derry Journal, 6 October 1937: no contests in any ward); the two ordinary vacancies: deemed re-elected, no nomination: 'Nationalists had made no nominations ... Councillors Andrew M'Closkey and William Quigley are the retiring Nationalist councillors in the West Ward, and Councillors B. Doherty and Frank Callaghan in the South. It is thought these may be automatically returned' (Derry Journal 6 Oct 1937 p5); confirmed on the cited page (round-2 final, 7 Nov 2026): the Nationalists 'had made no nominations', the Unionists were nominated only 'in the remaining three Wards' (North, East and Waterside), and the only other nomination was Mr. Michael M'Nutt's, 'to fill the extra vacancy created in the South Ward', so no one was nominated for the South Ward's two ordinary seats.

note: Annual retirement of two councillors in each of the five wards of Londonderry Corporation, held in October after the ordinary day was moved for 1937; nominations Tuesday 5 October 1937. The Nationalists made no nominations, holding the election pointless with the whole Corporation due to retire in May 1938 under the new wards scheme; their retiring South and West councillors (B. Doherty and Frank Callaghan; Andrew M'Closkey and William Quigley) were deemed re-elected with no nomination, which the round-2 gap-fill (7 Nov 2026) records as the election it was; Michael M'Nutt was nominated, unopposed, for an extra South Ward vacancy. The Unionist nominees in North, East and Waterside were returned unopposed and there was no poll (Derry Journal, 6 October 1937). Nominated, by the Derry Catholic Ex-Combatants' Association, of which he was treasurer, for the extra vacancy caused by the earlier resignation of Councillor P. Maxwell; for the ward's two ordinary vacancies no one was nominated, and the retiring councillors B. Doherty and Frank Callaghan were deemed re-elected (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). No party label is printed. Deemed re-elected (the two retiring councillors, B. Doherty and Frank Callaghan, for the ordinary vacancies, no nomination; Michael M'Nutt returned unopposed for the extra vacancy).
